title: WHEP answer rewrites payload types and header-extension IDs in SDP only, while consumer RTP keeps the router's values
test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'WHEP answer payload types follow the consumer': 'with consumers whose router payload types differ from the offer' (4 tests: 'answers the primary codec and its RTX (apt included) with the consumer payload types', 'answers the audio codec with the consumer payload type', 'writes the feedback the offer lists for the matching codec under the consumer payload type', 'keeps the consumer numbering where the offer uses those numbers for other codecs'), 'with an offer that already uses the router payload types' ('yields the same answer as before'), 'with consumers built by the mediasoup ortc code from config.MEDIA_CODECS' (5 tests: router numbering, Chromium offer with host VP8 and opus, Chromium offer with OBS H.264, Firefox offer, an offer numbered like the router); adapted: the 16 'answer matcher:' rows, 'negotiates every offered extension whose id equals the router id, with consistent ids', 'negotiates no extension for a Chrome-like offer ...', 'keeps the answered payload types and codecs when extensions and feedback are filtered'
proof: Payload-type half of the issue (the header-extension half was TASK-024). Decision: section-189067a43c5f50160f1b8635/Q-001 option (a), from answers.md. Before the fix, node --test tests/whep.test.js failed 17 of 122 tests (7 new, 10 adapted assertions that expected the offer's numbering). With consumers built by mediasoup's own ortc code from config.MEDIA_CODECS (router VP8 100, RTX 101 apt 100, H.264 42e01f 102, RTX 103 apt 102, opus 110), the answer to a Chromium 153 offer declared 'm=video ... 96 97' (apt=96) for a VP8 consumer sending 100/101, and '108 109' for an H.264 consumer sending 102/103. The audio answer said 111 while the consumer sent 110. buildActiveSection replaced each payload type and the RTX apt with the offer's in the SDP only. After the fix the answer writes consumer.rtpParameters.codecs as they are: m-line, rtpmap, fmtp, rtcp-fb and RTX apt equal the consumer's payload types in every test (VAL-034). The offer codec a consumer codec matches is still looked up, only to take the rtcp-fb the offer lists under its own number. An offer numbered like the router gets a byte-for-byte unchanged answer (pinned). All 122 whep tests, the 154 WHEP tests and npm test (929) pass; lint and typecheck pass (VAL-042). Browser check against the real server (own build and ports, lock held), lib/whep.js before and after. Chromium 153 and Firefox 155 accept every answer (setRemoteDescription resolves). Chromium playback is identical before and after: it plays for an offer numbered like the router and for an H.264 host (router 102 is H.264 in Chromium's offer). It decodes nothing for a VP8 host (router 100 is VP9 profile 2 in its offer) or for opus (110 is telephone-event there). Firefox's ICE to the loopback server failed in this environment even for a router-numbered offer. A two-peer test without the server showed that both browsers decode only on their own offer's payload types, whatever the answer says. So the SDP now matches the wire, but browser playback still needs the router's numbers to agree with the viewer's offer: option (b), option (c), or pinned router payload types. Owner decision, see TASK-025.md.
